sections.title: Present Subjunctive Mood
sections.content:
The Present Subjunctive is used after verbs like suggest, recommend, demand, insist, propose in that-clauses. The verb remains in base form, regardless of the subject.

Structure: Subject + suggest/demand/etc. + that + subject + base verb

4-5 Step Solution Method:
Step 1: Identify reporting verbs like suggest, recommend, insist, demand.
Step 2: Check for a 'that' clause.
Step 3: Use base form of the verb (no -s, no past form).
Step 4: Do not change verb according to subject.
Step 5: Confirm that the meaning shows suggestion or requirement.

Example:
I suggest that he go early.
They demanded that she be present.

sections.title: Past Subjunctive (Unreal Situations)
sections.content:
The Past Subjunctive mainly appears as 'were' in unreal or hypothetical situations.

Structure: If + subject + were

4-5 Step Solution Method:
Step 1: Identify a hypothetical or unreal situation.
Step 2: Focus on the if-clause.
Step 3: Use 'were' for all subjects (I/he/she/it).
Step 4: Use would/could/might in the main clause.
Step 5: Ensure the situation is contrary to fact.

Example:
If I were the leader, I would change the policy.

sections.title: It is High Time / It is About Time
sections.content:
After 'It is high time' or 'It is about time', we use Simple Past, but the meaning refers to the present or near future.

Structure: It is high time + subject + past verb

4-5 Step Solution Method:
Step 1: Identify the phrase 'high time' or 'about time'.
Step 2: Locate the subject that follows.
Step 3: Use Simple Past form of the verb.
Step 4: Do not use present tense.
Step 5: Confirm that the meaning implies delay.

Example:
It is high time we took action.

sections.title: Inverted Structures (Hardly, No Sooner, Scarcely)
sections.content:
When sentences begin with negative adverbs like hardly, no sooner, scarcely, inversion is required.

Structures:
Hardly had + subject + V3 when...
No sooner had + subject + V3 than...

4-5 Step Solution Method:
Step 1: Identify starting word (hardly, no sooner, scarcely).
Step 2: Invert auxiliary and subject.
Step 3: Use Past Perfect (had + V3).
Step 4: Use 'when' with hardly/scarcely, 'than' with no sooner.
Step 5: Keep the second clause in Simple Past.

Example:
Hardly had I reached the station when the train left.
No sooner had she arrived than it began to rain.

sections.title: Mixed Conditionals
sections.content:
Mixed conditionals combine different time references (past condition + present result).

Common Structure:
If + Past Perfect, would + base verb

4-5 Step Solution Method:
Step 1: Identify that the condition refers to past.
Step 2: Check that the result refers to present.
Step 3: Use had + V3 in the if-clause.
Step 4: Use would + base verb in the main clause.
Step 5: Confirm logical cause-effect relationship.

Example:
If she had studied harder, she would be successful now.

sections.title: Complex Perfect Forms (have had / had had)
sections.content:
'Have had' is Present Perfect of 'have' and shows possession or experience. 'Had had' is Past Perfect of 'have' and shows earlier past possession or experience.

4-5 Step Solution Method:
Step 1: Identify whether the time reference is present or past.
Step 2: Use have/has had for present perfect meaning.
Step 3: Use had had for earlier past action.
Step 4: Do not remove repeated 'had' automatically.
Step 5: Check context for clarity of time sequence.

Example:
I have had this phone for two years.
She had had dinner before I arrived.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1. Adding -s in subjunctive form.
2. Using present tense after 'high time'.
3. Forgetting inversion after hardly/no sooner.
4. Mixing time references incorrectly in mixed conditionals.
5. Removing one 'had' in 'had had' incorrectly.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Subjunctive uses base verb. High time takes Simple Past. Inversion requires auxiliary before subject. Mixed conditionals combine different time references. 'Have had' and 'had had' depend on context and time sequence.

tricks.title: Suggestion = Base Verb
tricks.explanation: After suggest, recommend, insist, use base verb in that-clause.
tricks.example: They suggested that he leave immediately.

tricks.title: High Time Rule
tricks.explanation: After 'high time', always use Simple Past.
tricks.example: It is high time we made a decision.

tricks.title: Hardly Pattern
tricks.example: Hardly had he entered when the phone rang.

tricks.title: No Sooner Pairing
tricks.example: No sooner had I sat down than the meeting began.

tricks.title: Mixed Time Clue
tricks.explanation: Past condition + present result = mixed conditional.
tricks.example: If I had prepared well, I would feel confident now.

tricks.title: Double Had Awareness
tricks.explanation: 'Had had' can be correct in past perfect context.
tricks.example: He had had enough practice before the match started.

tricks.title: Were for Formal Unreal
tricks.explanation: Use 'were' instead of 'was' in formal hypothetical clauses.
tricks.example: If she were here, she would guide us.

tricks.title: Inversion Alert Words
tricks.explanation: Never, rarely, hardly at the beginning require inversion.
tricks.example: Never have I seen such dedication.
